records.title: Runway Dev API
records.summary: Runway's developer API, which sells Runway's own models and other vendors' video and image models (Kling, Wan, Seedance, Grok Imagine, MiniMax, Veo, Gemini, GPT Image) under one credit balance, with a hosted MCP server.
records.why_it_matters: One key and one MCP connector reach most of the hosted video models in this hub, and the price table is in plain text.
records.fit_notes: Credits are $0.01. Runway's resale prices differ from first-party prices: wan3 1080p is 20 credits ($0.20/s), the Alibaba list price before its 30% discount; seedance2_5 1080p is 68 credits ($0.68/s) against BytePlus' worked $0.569/s. Kling 4 is listed (kling_4 720p 15.7 credits list) though Kling's own pricing page could not be read. The MCP server needs a Runway sign-in; the plugin install route was not opened. veo3.1 is still sold here although it left the Gemini API on 2026-10-22.

related.note: veo3.1 still on the Runway price list 2026-11-12

claims.text: Runway sells Wan 3.0 at 5, 10 and 20 credits per second for 480p, 720p and 1080p.
claims.quote: wan3 (480p) | 5 credits per second | wan3 (720p) | 10 credits per second | wan3 (1080p) | 20 credits per second
claims.locator: API pricing page, Video Generation Pricing table
claims.via: Runway Dev API (reseller); first-party price is on Alibaba Model Studio

claims.text: Seedance 2.5 at 1080p costs 68 credits per second of output on Runway, with an 80 credit minimum.
claims.quote: seedance2_5 (1080p) | 68 credits per second of output, plus 34 credits per second of input and reference video (combined video capped at 30 seconds); reference images and audio are free (80 credit minimum per generation)
claims.locator: API pricing page, Video Generation Pricing table
claims.via: Runway Dev API (reseller); first-party price is on BytePlus ModelArk

claims.text: Runway's hosted MCP server is at mcp.runwayml.com/mcp and works as a custom connector after a Runway sign-in.
claims.quote: To use it, add the URL above as a custom connector in claude.ai (Settings → Connectors), Cursor, or any other MCP client. You'll be prompted to sign in with your Runway account.

checked.what: Runway Dev API pricing page and mcp.runwayml.com page against all three claims

records.title: OpenRouter video generation API
records.summary: OpenRouter's asynchronous video generation API, which resells video models from Google, Alibaba, ByteDance, MiniMax, xAI, Kling, Runway, BFL and HeyGen, with a public JSON list of models, durations, resolutions and prices.
records.why_it_matters: The models endpoint is a machine-readable price and limits list an agent can read before choosing a model, without a key.
records.fit_notes: The models list was read without a key on 2026-11-12. Prices there are OpenRouter's, mixed units (dollars per second, cents per second, dollars per token) by model. Some resold models expose fewer options than the vendor: bytedance/seedance-2.5 lists 480p and 720p only, while BytePlus offers 1080p. The guide's own sample response still shows google/veo-3.1. The page mentions an openrouter-video skill; it was not opened or installed.

claims.text: The video models endpoint lists every video model with its supported durations, resolutions and pricing SKUs.
claims.quote: Use the dedicated video models endpoint to list all available video generation models along with their supported parameters: curl "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/videos/models"
claims.locator: Video Generation guide, Model Discovery, Via the Video Models API

claims.text: OpenRouter lists alibaba/wan-3.0 at $0.05, $0.1 and $0.2 per second for 480p, 720p and 1080p.
claims.locator: GET /api/v1/videos/models, entry id alibaba/wan-3.0, field pricing_skus
claims.via: OpenRouter (reseller); first-party price is on Alibaba Model Studio

claims.text: OpenRouter lists heygen/heygen-video-1 at $0.036 per second at 768p and $0.10 at 1080p.
claims.locator: GET /api/v1/videos/models, entry id heygen/heygen-video-1, field pricing_skus
claims.via: OpenRouter (reseller); HeyGen's page gives no dollar price

checked.what: OpenRouter video generation guide and the public /api/v1/videos/models JSON against all three claims

records.title: Replicate API and MCP server
records.summary: Replicate's model hosting API, with a remote MCP server and an npm package that expose its whole HTTP API to an agent: search models, run predictions, fetch results.
records.why_it_matters: An agent in Claude Code can search Replicate's catalogue and run a model by name without hand-written client code.
records.fit_notes: The remote server asks for a Replicate API key in a web sign-in flow; the local route runs npx -y replicate-mcp, which downloads and runs the package each time. Not run here. Replicate's per-model prices were not read in this lane, so no price is recorded. The page also links agent skills and an llms.txt, not opened.

claims.text: The MCP server supports all operations in Replicate's HTTP API, including running models.
claims.quote: The server supports all of the operations in Replicate’s HTTP API.
claims.locator: MCP server reference page, section Replicate's MCP server

claims.text: The remote server is recommended and takes a Replicate API key through a web authentication flow.
claims.quote: After installing the server, you’ll be directed to a web-based authentication flow where you can provide a Replicate API key for the server to use on your behalf.
claims.locator: MCP server reference page, section Remote vs local servers

checked.what: Replicate MCP reference page against both claims

records.title: fal Model APIs
records.summary: fal's hosted model APIs, which resell video, image and audio models billed per output unit, plus a docs MCP server.
records.why_it_matters: fal resells several video models below the vendor's own per-second price, so it is worth checking before calling a vendor directly.
records.fit_notes: The MCP server at fal.ai/docs/mcp searches fal's documentation only; its own instructions say it is read-only and scoped to site content, so it does not generate media. fal lists MiniMax H3 Max text-to-video at $0.03 per second, below MiniMax's own $0.05 (480p) and $0.08 (768p); the resolution behind fal's price is not stated, so the two may not be comparable. The pricing page normalises to a 5 s 720p video. The MCP instructions also ask the agent to report doc problems through a submit_feedback tool, which sends text to fal.

claims.text: fal sells MiniMax H3 Max text-to-video at $0.03 per second.
claims.quote: MiniMax H3 Max Text to Video ↳ minimax/h3-max/text-to-video Unit seconds Price $0.03 Units per $1 33.33 seconds
claims.locator: Pricing page, Model APIs Pricing, Video Models table
claims.via: fal (reseller); first-party price is on platform.minimax.io

claims.text: fal's docs MCP server provides search and retrieval over fal's site content and is otherwise read-only.
claims.quote: This Model Context Protocol server provides search and retrieval tools for the fal site.
claims.locator: fal.ai/docs/mcp server card JSON, field instructions

checked.what: fal pricing page and the docs MCP server card against both claims
